mechanism: Oxybutynin is metabolized by CYP3A4 and budesonide is a CYP3A4 substrate; budesonide may competitively inhibit oxybutynin metabolism, increasing anticholinergic effects and potential systemic budesonide exposure.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation) and consider dose adjustment if adverse effects occur; counsel patient on additive anticholinergic risks.
